## Summary

**PSUB** (Vector subtract): Vector subtract.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `b – a → d` |
| Syntax | `PSUBB <vea>,b,d`<br>`PSUBW <vea>,b,d`<br>`PSUBUSB <vea>,b,d`<br>`PSUBUSW <vea>,b,d` |
| Short | Vector subtract. |
| Description | Psubb is 8byte vector, It calculates 8 subtractions. Psubw is 4 word vector. This is for 4 subtractions. Unsigned Saturated has a lower limit and an upper limit. When the result is below zero it is clipped to be zero. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–9 | `1111111` |
| 1 | 8 | A |
| 1 | 7 | B |
| 1 | 6 | D |
| 1 | 5–3 | Mode |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–12 | b |
| 2 | 11–8 | d |
| 2 | 7–3 | `00010` |
| 2 | 2 | U |
| 2 | 1 | `1` |
| 2 | 0 | S |

- S=Size 0=byte, 1=word.
- U=1 Unsigned Saturated else signed & no limiting.

### Example

```asm
    psubb    d0,d1,d2
```

```text
vea d0: 01 23 45 67 89 AB 04 12
b d1: 04 12 01 02 FF 05 01 23
Result:
d d2: 03 EF BC 9B 76 5A FD 11
Result of psubusb d0,d1,d2:
d d2: 03 00 00 00 76 00 00 11
Result of psubusw d0,d1,d2:
d d2: 02 EF 00 00 75 5A 00 00
```

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have no PSUB. It is new on the 68080.

## Do / Don't

- No rules beyond the details above.
